steps.title: The VDP
steps.body: The VDP, Verband Deutscher Prädikatsweingüter, is an association of about 200 top German estates, founded in 1910. Its emblem is an eagle with grapes on the bottle capsule. The Rheingau's Charta association, from 1984, pioneered dry, food-friendly Riesling and site classification, ideas the VDP adopted nationally.

steps.title: Four levels
steps.body: The VDP's pyramid, like Burgundy's, has four levels: Gutswein, estate wine; Ortswein, village wine; Erste Lage, first-class site; and Grosse Lage, great site. Dry wines from Grosse Lage sites are called Grosses Gewächs, GG. Sweet wines from top sites still use Prädikat terms, like Spätlese or Auslese.

steps.prompt: Order the VDP levels from broadest to most precise.
steps.explanation: Each step narrows the origin and raises the standard.

steps.title: Why it matters
steps.body: German wine law ranks wine by grape ripeness, not by site. The VDP's private classification brings site to the centre, as in Burgundy. Rheingau sites like Rüdesheimer Berg Schlossberg, Erbacher Marcobrunn and Hochheimer Hölle are Grosse Lage. Not all great producers are VDP members.

options: A dry wine from a Grosse Lage site
steps.explanation: GG marks the VDP's top dry wines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The VDP is an association of about 200 top estates
Its pyramid runs from Gutswein to Grosse Lage
Grosses Gewächs is a dry wine from a top site
